To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the absorptive capacity and customer involvement of a firm are positively related to the benefits and challenges associated with the development of a radical innovation.
the absorptive capacity (both potential and realized) of spin offs affects the challenges and benefits of customer involvement in radical innovation development.

the blending capability of a spin off is the capability to simultaneously develop both market and technical knowledge through both market pull and technology-push approaches, and to involve both customers and parent research center, and to develop both potential and realized capabilities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how firms can effectively manage customer involvement in the context of radical innovation.
the role of customers in the development of technological innovations, and the role of the parent research center as a knowledge source.
the absorptive capacity for customer involvement in the context of radical innovation in spin offs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the blending capability of spin offs is a key factor in the development of successful radical innovations.
the blending capability of spin offs is a critical determinant of the success of customer involvement in developing radical innovations.

customer involvement in the early stage of the development of a radical innovation is important, but it needs to be balanced with the involvement of the parent research center and with the development of absorptive capacity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the absorptive capacity is a key factor for the success of customer involvement in radical innovation development.
the absorptive capacity and blending capability are critical for spin offs in the development of their radical innovation.
customer involvement in the innovation process of spin offs is a complex process that is influenced by a number of factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that

spin offs should develop both potential and realized capabilities to absorb customer knowledge and technology awareness to balance between market and technical knowledge in the development of new radical technologies.
customer involvement in the early phases of the innovation process is not a one size fits all solution.

spin offs should not only develop absorptive capacities, but also develop the blending capability to balance the market and technical knowledge as well as the involvement of customers with parent research centers.
